title: Brain region-resolved pharmacodynamics of an antisense oligonucleotide targeting human SNCA 3′UTR in BAC-hSNCA rats
title_zh: 针对人类SNCA 3′UTR的反义寡核苷酸在BAC-hSNCA大鼠中的脑区分辨药效动力学
abstract: Abstract Background Alpha-synuclein accumulation contributes to Parkinson’s disease (PD), and lowering α-synuclein expression is a candidate disease-modifying approach. The brain-wide pharmacodynamic profile of human-targeting antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) remains incompletely defined in humanized models that preserve the regulatory architecture of the human SNCA locus. Methods BAC-h SNCA rats were treated at an early stage, when human α-synuclein is elevated, but striatal dopamine content remains largely preserved. A single intracerebroventricular dose of an ASO targeting human SNCA 3′UTR (SNCA ASO3.0) was administered, and outcomes were assessed 45 days later by isoform-specific RT-qPCR, immunoblotting of soluble and detergent-insoluble α-synuclein species, bulk RNA-seq across selected regions, multiplex cytokine profiling, phospho-kinase assays, neurotransmitter quantification, and behavioral testing. Results SNCA ASO3.0 reduced human SNCA mRNA and multiple α-synuclein protein species in a regionally graded manner, with the strongest effects in the olfactory bulb and striatum. Bulk RNA-seq identified anatomically distinct transcriptional responses, including synaptic and metabolic pathway shifts in the olfactory bulbs and immune-related enrichment within glial signatures in the striatum and midbrain, without detectable changes in protein levels of glial fibrillary acidic protein or ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1. Cytokine profiling showed selective modulation of a subset of analytes, and phospho-kinase assays indicated reduced AKT1S1/PRAS40 phosphorylation. Striatal dopamine levels were unchanged, whereas the striatal tyrosine hydroxylase level was increased. SNCA ASO3.0 increased locomotor activity and improved exploratory behavior and selected measures of olfactory discrimination. Conclusions Partial suppression of human α-synuclein in a humanized rat model yields region-specific molecular adaptations accompanied by early behavioral changes at a stage preceding overt dopamine depletion. These data provide a framework for evaluating region-resolved consequences of α-synuclein-lowering interventions in synucleinopathies.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景：α-突触核蛋白（α-synuclein）积累是帕金森病（PD）的致病因素之一，降低α-突触核蛋白表达被视为一种潜在的疾病修饰策略。针对人类SNCA基因的反义寡核苷酸（ASO）的全脑药效动力学特征在保留人类SNCA位点调控结构的人源化模型中尚未完全阐明。方法：在早期阶段（人类α-突触核蛋白升高但纹状体多巴胺含量基本保持）对BAC-hSNCA大鼠进行处理。单次脑室内注射针对人类SNCA 3′UTR的ASO（SNCA ASO3.0），并在45天后通过亚型特异性RT-qPCR、可溶性与去垢剂不溶性α-突触核蛋白免疫印迹、选定脑区的全转录组测序、细胞因子多重测定、磷酸化激酶检测、神经递质定量以及行为测试评估结果。结果：SNCA ASO3.0在脑区梯度上降低了人类SNCA mRNA及多种α-突触核蛋白，最显著的效应出现在嗅球和纹状体。全转录组测序揭示了解剖学上不同的转录响应，包括嗅球的突触与代谢通路转变，以及纹状体和中脑的胶质细胞谱系中免疫相关富集，但未检测到胶质纤维酸性蛋白或离子化钙结合适配蛋白1的蛋白水平变化。细胞因子分析显示部分分析物的选择性调节，磷酸化激酶检测提示AKT1S1/PRAS40磷酸化下降。纹状体多巴胺水平未变，而纹状体酪氨酸羟化酶水平升高。SNCA ASO3.0提升了运动活性，改善了探索行为和部分嗅觉辨别测量。结论：在人源化大鼠模型中部分抑制人类α-突触核蛋白可产生脑区特异的分子适应，并在明显多巴胺耗竭前的早期阶段伴随行为改变。这些数据为评估α-突触核蛋白降低干预在突触核蛋白病中的脑区分辨后果提供了框架。
